criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-git`. A test starts two writers at once (threads) against one repository, with different record paths. Both land, each path is present on the final tip, every update was a fast-forward (each tip descends from the previous one), and no commit was lost.
criteria.evidence: two_simultaneous_writers_both_land_as_fast_forwards passed. It starts two scoped threads behind a Barrier, and each writes a different path with unwrap. It then asserts that both paths are in ls_tree of the tip, that the chain holds 2 commits containing both outcomes' commits, that the first commit has no parent, and that the second commit's only parent is the first. The plan said 3 commits (a root plus 2), but the root here is the first writer's own commit. So 2 is correct, and no commit was lost.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-git`. A test makes the ref move between the writer's read and its update (a stale expected tip). The first update is rejected, the writer refetches and replays its new files on the new tip, and the write succeeds. The earlier commit and the new files are both in the final tree.
criteria.evidence: a_rejected_update_refetches_replays_and_succeeds passed. On attempt 1 the before_update hook lands a rival commit. The test then asserts attempts == 2, that the final commit's parent is the rival's commit, and that the tree holds both mine.json and theirs.json. A further test, a_replay_refuses_when_the_winner_took_the_same_path, covers the assumption that the existing-path check runs again on each attempt.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-git`. Tests show that a write that modifies an existing path, deletes one, or renames one (a delete plus an add of the same content) is refused with an error. In each case the branch tip after the call equals the tip before. A write with identical bytes at an existing path is also tested, and its result is documented.
criteria.evidence: a_write_that_changes_an_existing_path_is_refused_and_the_tip_stays passed. Seven writes are each asserted to fail with Err(GitError::Refused) and to leave the tip unchanged: modify, delete, rename, identical bytes, file over directory, directory over file, and a duplicate path. The identical-bytes case is refused, and that result is documented in a test comment, the module docs, the CHANGELOG and the design doc.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-git`. A test shows that `athena/records` shares no history with main: `git merge-base main athena/records` finds nothing, and the first records commit has no parent. A second test shows the retry bound is enforced. When every attempt is rejected, the writer returns a clear error after the bounded count and does not loop.
criteria.evidence: the_branch_is_its_own_root_with_no_history_in_common_with_main passed. It asserts that merge-base exits 1 with empty stdout, that the first commit has no parents, and that main holds only a.txt. the_retry_bound_is_enforced also passed: with max_attempts 3 and the hook moving the ref every time, the hook runs exactly 3 times, the error contains 'all 3 attempts', and the tip holds only the three rival files.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean. `cargo test` passes for the workspace.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree: `cargo fmt --all --check` passed, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` passed, and `cargo test --locked` passed (1027 tests).

It uses the existing Git wrapper, temp index and commit_tree helpers, with no new crate. A repository search finds no caller of it outside athena-git, so the pipeline is untouched.

The two-threads test does not force contention, so it may pass without either writer being rejected.
findings.evidence: In two_simultaneous_writers_both_land_as_fast_forwards, the Barrier lines the two threads up, but nothing guarantees that one thread's compare-and-swap is rejected. The reject-and-replay path is covered deterministically by a_rejected_update_refetches_replays_and_succeeds, so no criterion is left unshown.

summary: The change passes. It adds `athena_git::records_branch::RecordsWriter`, which writes opaque record files to `athena/records` as a branch with its own root. The ref moves with a compare-and-swap (`git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`), and a rejected update re-reads the tip and retries up to a set bound, 5 by default. Any write that would modify, delete or rename an existing path is refused, including one with identical bytes, and the tip does not move. I ran `cargo test -p athena-git records_branch` and all 7 new tests passed. Together they cover two simultaneous writers, a rejection followed by a successful replay, the refusal cases, no shared history with main (merge-base exits 1), and the retry bound (exactly 3 attempts, then a clear error). For fmt, clippy and the workspace tests I relied on Athena's recorded passes for this tree; I did not rerun them. All five changed files are on the deliverables list, the only caller-free search hits are inside athena-git and the docs, no crate is added, and no governance or records/ file is touched. One nit: the two-threads test does not guarantee the threads actually collide, but a separate test forces a rejection and covers the retry path.
